fd_note: Frame 1 is the frame the button was pressed. A tick (✓) means the script measured that value by playing the move and it matched the design; every measured value matched. Startup, active and recovery are design values. The tests check that no hit ever lands outside the active frames. Light 1's window opens on frame 8, but a target straight ahead is first hit on frame 10: the cut starts on the right side and reaches the front 2 frames later.
tun_caption: Hits missed on thin targets (5–15 cm radius) that a 256-sample check catches, across all four attacks.
tun_text: A strike moves the sword tip more than a metre between frames. Checked once per frame, the blade missed 370 of the 456 thin targets it actually passed through. Four checks per frame still missed 146. The build spaces checks by how far the tip moved, at most 5 cm apart. That's about 30 checks in an active frame and none outside, and it missed 2. The whole simulation, hit checks included, costs 0.021 ms a frame.
rate_caption: Presses that landed on a different frame from the 60 Hz run, reading input once per display frame. With timestamped input: 0 at every rate.
rate_title: Input read once per display frame changes the fight at 6 of 7 refresh rates
rate_text: The same 40-second scripted fight was played at seven display rates. Reading input once per display frame, like polling in Update(), moved presses by up to 3 frames and changed the outcome: at 30 Hz the player landed 23 hits instead of 24; at 120 Hz they took 3 hits instead of 4. Applying each key event to the frame it happened in gave the identical fight, frame for frame, at 7 of 7 rates.
blend_caption: Largest joint rotation in the single frame where the move changes, over 126 transitions in the scripted fight.
blend_title: Blends remove the pose jumps, except dodge cancels, which snap on purpose
blend_text: With hard cuts, 42 of 126 transitions turned a joint more than 45° in one frame. With blends, 3 did, and all of them were dodges cancelling out of an attack. The dodge blends in over 2 frames on purpose, because a dodge that eases in feels late. For scale, the strikes themselves turn a joint up to 102° a frame. Light 2 was keyed to start where Light 1 ends, so that chain barely moves even without a blend.
swing_caption: Startup, active and recovery frames for each attack (taller cells are active). The marker is the frame where the sword tip moves fastest.
swing_title: The fastest part of every swing lands inside its active frames
swing_text: If the blade is still accelerating when the hit window closes, players see a hit that didn't count. For 4 of 4 attacks the tip's fastest frame falls inside the active window, and 46–62% of the tip's whole path is covered while the blade can hit. The rest is wind-up, follow-through and the return to guard.
